theme: An open Saturday in Portland — the week's overdue decisions wait for tomorrow's review.
greeting: The girls are with Jen this week, Dan, so today was mostly yours: one concert at midday and otherwise open. The real work is tomorrow's 15-minute review, where a few travel calls have run out of room to slip.

needsAttention.title: Sunday review reopens the board
needsAttention.detail: Your 15-minute review with Mike is where the overdue items below get owners and dates. Come ready to kill or commit on the travel calls rather than let them slip a fourth Sunday.

needsAttention.title: Maine Christmas SUV won't wait
needsAttention.detail: A full-size SUV out of Portland over Christmas week sells out, and this has been flagged 'book this week' since mid-September. A refundable hold now costs nothing and removes the whole risk.

needsAttention.title: December trip decision is due
needsAttention.detail: The decision was set for Sep 30 and booking for Oct 15 — holiday inventory for six over three weeks is the thinnest of the year. Pick domestic vs. international and book refundable.

needsAttention.title: Pathfinder drive is this week
needsAttention.detail: The Oct 5–18 gap between girl-weeks is the window to drive the Pathfinder from Portland to St. Pete; book the single hotel night once the dates are set.

flagged.title: A Citi managing-director role surfaced
flagged.detail: LinkedIn flagged Head of Business Development, USCC, MD at Citi — a scan-worthy lead for the search.

flagged.title: Fran's lunch still needs a venue
flagged.detail: Friday 12:30 is set; she's happy with sushi if there are cooked options, and is waiting on you to name the place.

inbox.noise: Otherwise just newsletters and promos — Dermstore, a St. Pete weekend roundup, Patreon, Academia.

recipe.title: Quinces Poached in Muscat
recipe.why: Autumn is quince season, and poaching coaxes the hard fruit into something fragrant and tender.

tasks.title: Portland house order — bedframe + shower soap holder

acts.line: A slow, unscheduled start — nothing on the calendar before midday.
The middle of the day had its one commitment downtown; everything around it was yours.
Quiet now — the overdue board is tomorrow's job, not tonight's.
